note: NECO Civic Education round 5 (R49 top-up): creativity; cooperation; perseverance; critical thinking; communication skills; leadership qualities; limitations of rights; inalienable rights; PVC; one man one vote; voting age 18; sex education; school as agent of socialization; press as watchdog; national ethics; social justice; quota system; English as official language; the diaspora; oath of office; conflict of interest; democratic values; vigilante groups; widows' inheritance rights; birth registration. Scanned against the whole Civic pool (JAMB, WAEC and NECO stems) and cleared of cross-subject twins (Gov, Econ, CA, CRS, IRS, Agric, Use of English).

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The value shown by a student who finds a new, better way of solving an old classroom problem is
questions.explanation: He refuses to walk the old road when a new one can be cut.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: When members of a community come together to dig their well, each person working beside the others, the value they display is
questions.explanation: Many hands, one well, one joy.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: A trader who keeps retrying her business after three failed attempts, refusing to give up, displays the value of
questions.explanation: She falls seven times and rises eight.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Before accepting a rumour forwarded on WhatsApp, a good citizen first examines the evidence and asks whether it is true. This habit of examining before believing is called
questions.explanation: The mind that asks questions is harder to deceive.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The ability to pass information clearly and to listen carefully to others, which every class prefect needs, is called
questions.explanation: A leader who cannot be understood cannot lead.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: A good leader, besides being honest and hardworking, must be able to
questions.D: inspire and guide those he leads
questions.explanation: Leadership is lifting others, not standing on them.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: During a declared emergency, the law may place certain limits on a citizen's freedom of movement. This shows that citizens' rights are
questions.B: limited by law in the public interest
questions.C: granted by the police at will
questions.explanation: Even the freest river has banks.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Fundamental human rights are described as inalienable because they
questions.A: are sold to the highest bidder
questions.C: cannot be taken away from a person
questions.explanation: No government can lawfully peel them from a human being.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The document that a registered Nigerian voter must present at the polling unit before being allowed to vote is the
questions.explanation: No card, no vote — the rule is simple.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The principle that every citizen's vote carries the same weight, so that no voter counts more than another, is expressed as
questions.explanation: The professor's vote and the labourer's weigh the same.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: For a person to be qualified to vote in a Nigerian election, the person must, among other things, have attained the age of
questions.explanation: The law hands the ballot to adulthood.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Schools include sex education in the curriculum chiefly to help young people
questions.B: avoid every other subject in school
questions.D: make informed choices about their bodies
questions.explanation: Knowledge guards the young better than silence.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Besides the family and the peer group, the institution where children are formally taught the knowledge, skills and values of their society is the
questions.explanation: The teacher stands beside the parent in shaping the child.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The press is often called the watchdog of society because it
questions.A: barks at strangers on the street
questions.B: guards the bank vaults at night
questions.explanation: A barking press scares away the thieves of public trust.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The 1999 Constitution names the national ethics of Nigeria as discipline, integrity, dignity of labour, social justice, religious tolerance and
questions.explanation: Six simple words carry the nation's conscience.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The principle of social justice demands that the wealth, opportunities and burdens of society be
questions.explanation: Justice means nobody's share is stolen by another's power.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The quota system, used in admissions and employment, allots places to people from different states or regions mainly to
questions.C: ensure that every group gets a fair share
questions.explanation: The national cake is cut so every table receives a slice.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Because Nigeria has over five hundred languages, the language adopted for official business, schools and the civil service is
questions.explanation: One borrowed tongue speaks for many native ones.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Nigerians living abroad — the doctors, engineers and traders in America, Europe and elsewhere — are collectively referred to as the Nigerian
questions.explanation: Scattered like salt, yet still of the same shaker.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Public officers take the oath of office at the start of their tenure mainly to
questions.A: pledge faithful service to the nation
questions.explanation: The tongue promises what the term must perform.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: A commissioner who awards a road contract to a construction company owned by his own brother, without disclosing it, is guilty of
questions.explanation: Public power was used to fill a private pocket.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Values such as tolerance of opposition, respect for the rule of law and willingness to compromise, which keep democracy alive, are collectively called
questions.explanation: Democracy stands on the habits of its people.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: In many Nigerian communities, young men organise themselves into ____ groups to guard the neighbourhood at night. Unchecked, such groups can turn to lawlessness, which is why the police do not encourage them.
questions.explanation: A double-edged guard: protection today, menace tomorrow.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: In some communities a widow is denied her late husband's property, which is seized by his relatives. This practice violates her
questions.explanation: Her marriage did not cancel her ownership.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The registration of a child's birth at the national population office soon after the child is born is important because the record
questions.A: proves the child's identity and nationality
questions.B: guarantees the child a government job
questions.D: earns the parents a monthly grant
questions.explanation: A certificate no bigger than a hand carries a whole life's beginning.
